hero.headline: Flashing traffic light at Glades Cut Off Road still not operational after 6 months
hero.body:
A flashing traffic light installed at the intersection of Glades Cut Off Road and Commerce Center Drive more than six months ago remains not fully operational, and neighbors say the confusion it creates is becoming a safety concern. The light was installed by the Wylder community in December. St. Lucie County said the light still needs to align with the Florida East Coast Railway track signals before it can be fully operational.

Brian Packard, who lives near the intersection, said the light has made some difference but not enough. Taylor Lorsten said the flashing mode creates more problems than it solves. Lorsten said drivers do not know how to respond to the light and people stop when they should not stop or go when they should not go. More than six months after installation, Lorsten said she has not seen any work being done on the light.

Lorsten said the flashing light adds major backups and worries that confused, aggressive driving could put her family at risk. Her son is a new driver. Packard said the situation remains dangerous.

The answer remains unclear as to who is responsible for making the light fully operational. Lorsten said it is not clear whose responsibility it is and what time frame that would fit into. Efforts to reach the Wylder community, FEC Railways and St. Lucie County were ongoing.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents raise concerns over proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum. Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County history, said the museum is a gem for the area and the center for the county's culture.

Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings. St. Lucie County said no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce pizza shop transforms patio into free reading room for children
cards.teaser: Big Apple Pizza owner Scott Van Duzer is expanding the restaurant's free book program by transforming its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up a book any time they visit.
cards.body:
For years, Van Duzer has kept shelves of free books inside the restaurant at 2311 S 35th St in Fort Pierce, inviting children to take one home at no cost. He said seeing kids light up when they discover a new book has been one of the most rewarding parts of the program. As more children have stopped by to pick up books, the collection has continued to grow. Van Duzer said the restaurant has simply run out of space inside, prompting the decision to turn the outdoor patio into a permanent reading room.

The goal is to make books easy to access and help encourage a lifelong love of reading. Whether a family comes in for pizza or simply stops by for a book, every child is welcome to take one home. Van Duzer said giving back has always been part of the restaurant's mission and that commitment comes from the example his mother set while he was growing up. Construction on the new reading room is underway and is expected to be completed later this fall.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police seek help identifying suspects in vandalism, vehicle burglary cases
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are asking for the public's help identifying people shown in surveillance images connected to two separate investigations involving vandalism and vehicle burglaries.
cards.body:
Police said the vandalism occurred at about 4 p.m. July 24 at the Fort Pierce Recreation Center, located at 903 S. An unidentified woman was captured on camera damaging city property. Multiple air-conditioning units, a trailer and a storage shed were damaged.

The second investigation involves a series of vehicle burglaries reported during the overnight hours of July 27 in the Lawnwood Circle area. Police said the burglaries occurred in the 1300 block of Nebraska Avenue and the 1300 block of Peppertree Trail, primarily between 2 a.m. and dawn. Investigators said several vehicles were burglarized. Some had been left unlocked, while others had windows smashed to gain entry. Surveillance footage showed several people in the area wearing hoodies, shorts and backpacks. Anyone who recognizes the people pictured or has information about either case is asked to contact Fort Pierce police. Anonymous tips can be submitted to Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at tcwatch.org.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash during armed robbery at Fort Pierce Wells Fargo ATM
cards.teaser: A man using a Wells Fargo ATM became the victim of an armed robbery after two men forced him to pull out cash before fleeing the scene on foot.
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department said the robbery happened Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. Two men approached the victim, and one of them displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash. Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the scene, established a perimeter and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects.

The suspects were not located. Police described them as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie men flee police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: Two men led Port St. Lucie police on a high-speed chase before abandoning their car and fleeing on foot Monday, with one suspect found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving on Southwest Becker Road. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated and weaved in and out of traffic, ignoring traffic signs and signals.

 The driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

 The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station on Tradition commercial site after months of resident concerns
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Driv
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in Tradition. The council unanimously approved the restriction on July 13 as part of the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development, ending nearly three months of debate over the future of land originally planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development.

 Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission in May to convert the parcel from residential to commercial use. While council members supported commercial development, several raised concerns that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use, leading the council to table the request on May 26. Heritage Oaks residents urged the council in June to reject the land-use change, citing traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts.

 The council voted 4-0 on June 22 to approve the commercial designation after the developer agreed to permanently give up the right to build a gas station. The July 13 ordinance codified that restriction into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring the prohibition remains with the property regardless of future ownership. City planner Bridget Kean said service stations remain permitted elsewhere in the Tradition mixed-use area but are now prohibited on Parcel 11A. The updated plan also requires the developer to install a fence along the southern property line before mass grading and to complete an architectural wall and landscape buffering along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued.

 Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the public process and the decision, saying Port St. Lucie has long lacked commercial development, placing a burden on homeowners. Councilman David Pickett said the city has consistently heard residents oppose additional housing and called the shift to commercial the best outcome for the corner. Councilwoman Stephanie Morgan, who initially questioned whether prohibiting a specific business type amounted to government interference, ultimately voted with the council. Mayor Shannon Martin confirmed the restriction would remain with the property in perpetuity before the final unanimous vote.

hero.headline: Indian River County firefighter and paramedic died by suicide in Sebastian, police report reveals
hero.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue firefighter and paramedic Geoffrey S. Lang, 35, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound at his Sebastian home on Saturday, July 25, according to a Sebastian Police Department report released Wednesday. Officers responded to Lang's residence at 4:18 p.m. after his wife called 911 to report that her husband had shot himself in front of her.

Sebastian police officers arrived to find Lang's wife and a neighbor outside the residence. Officers entered the home with a K-9 dog and discovered Lang's body in a bedroom with an apparent gunshot wound to the head. An Indian River County Fire Rescue individual pronounced Lang dead at the scene. His body was transported to the medical examiner's office by Lowther Funeral Home.

A neighbor told police they heard a woman yelling and screaming, followed by a single gunshot between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. The neighbor initially thought the sound was fireworks but recognized it as a gunshot. After officers arrived, one neighbor reported speaking with a female neighbor who appeared hostile.

A funeral service for Lang will be held Tuesday, August 3, at Community Church located at 1901 23rd Street. Anyone needing help can contact the Suicide Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988, or reach the 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast by dialing 211 or texting their ZIP code to 898211.

Indian River County Fire Rescue firefighters spent Tuesday, July 28, at Dodgertown Elementary at 4350 43rd Street in Vero Beach for a career fair. Firefighters shared what it is like to serve the community and introduced students to careers in the fire service.

Firefighters answered questions from students and showed off equipment during the event. Fire Rescue said it was a day of learning and inspiration for the students.

cards.headline: Recycled fishing line becomes friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art Aug. 8
cards.teaser: Discarded fishing line will be transformed into friendship bracelets when the Vero Beach Museum of Art teams up with Coastal Connections for a free Second Saturday program beginnin
cards.body:
Discarded fishing line will be transformed into friendship bracelets when the Vero Beach Museum of Art teams up with Coastal Connections for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8. Coastal Connections will lead the hands-on activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium, where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways.

 Participants can also learn about the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

 The event includes docent-led mini-tours, studio art projects and opportunities to learn about protecting local marine life. From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can then participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions.

 Guests can also tour the museum's summer exhibitions throughout the day. James Prosek: At Work is on view in the Holmes Gallery, while Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases is displayed in the Schumann and Titelman galleries. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day.

 Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership is an example of working with the community to introduce everyone to marine conservation and environmental protection. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment. Additional programs may include performances, lectures, films and other arts and humanities offerings on select Saturdays.

cards.headline: 3 arrested in Fort Pierce after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in home with boarded windows, cockroaches
cards.teaser: Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile
cards.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile home in August 2025, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The infant's mother, Nicole Maxwell, 27, her father Robert Maxwell, 61, and his girlfriend Vikki Koon, 38, were arrested last week following an 11-month investigation.

 Nicole Maxwell was arrested on July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street SW in Vero Beach and is being held in Indian River County Jail on no bond. Robert Maxwell and Koon are in St. Lucie County Jail each on a $1.5 million bond.

 St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Detective Jennifer Diaz said the investigation began when Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the infant to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital already deceased on Aug. 20, 2025. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach.

 Diaz, who has 20 years of law enforcement experience, called it one of the worst cases she has ever worked. The mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce had windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring and live and dead cockroaches throughout, according to court documents. The house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and was unsafe for walking, Diaz said.

 According to court documents, Koon primarily fed the infant only twice a day and admitted to investigators that when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in. She told deputies she believed a newborn should have two ounces per feeding twice a day. Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach while the child lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon.

 In the days before the death, Koon and Robert Maxwell messaged the child's mother and biological father, who lives in Virginia, stating they needed to come because the baby had marks all over him. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the conditions firsthand and that the home looked unlivable. She said other children in the home would come to her asking for water and appeared thirsty and unwashed, wearing the same clothes every day.

 Four other children of Nicole Maxwell who were living in the mobile home, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, have been placed in foster care through the Department of Children and Families. The medical examiner ruled the death a homicide. Diaz said the case took nearly a year to prosecute because it was complex and required outside experts to provide examinations, which can take several weeks or months. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said protecting children is a responsibility shared by the entire community and urged anyone who sees signs of child neglect or abuse to report it immediately.

cards.headline: Cyclist rides through Vero Beach on 2,600-mile journey from Key West to Maine
cards.teaser: A Boston cyclist rode through Vero Beach this week on a 2,600-mile bike ride from Key West to Maine to honor a friend lost to colorectal cancer.
cards.body:
Jay Weedall traveled to South Florida to begin the journey, with a goal of raising $50,000 for the Young Onset Colorectal Cancer Research Center. Weedall began his journey in Key West, pedaling 155 miles to Miami on day one. He set off on his second leg, a 163-mile ride to Vero Beach, after filling his hydration pack with ice to stay cool.

 Weedall is riding roughly 150 miles a day up the coast through nearly every state all the way to the Pan Mass Challenge. He will do the Pan Mass Challenge across Massachusetts on August 2 and continue to the Canadian border in Maine. By avoiding highways, Weedall says the route offers something unexpected, allowing him to experience little coastal towns along the inlets. Fans can follow Weedall's journey on the cycling app Strava.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Police Department honors service of Indian River County firefighter
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands with Indian River County Fire Rescue following the death of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning the loss of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang, who passed away while off duty. The department said its thoughts are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time and that it honors his service and the impact he made on the community.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue announced Lang's death Saturday night and thanked neighboring agencies that quickly shared messages of support following the announcement. The Sebastian Police Department said it stands alongside its brothers and sisters of Indian River County Fire Rescue as they mourn the heartbreaking loss and that Lang's dedication, courage and commitment to serving others will never be forgotten.
